neet_che_u03_t12_1.working: An antibonding MO comes from destructive overlap of the atomic orbitals. It has a node between the nuclei and lies above the parent atomic orbitals, so it destabilises the molecule.

neet_che_u03_t12_2.working: A pi orbital has a nodal plane that contains the internuclear axis. The pi* orbital also has an extra nodal plane between the nuclei. The sigma orbitals have no nodal plane containing the axis.

neet_che_u03_t12_3.working: Because of overlap and repulsion effects, the antibonding MO is raised in energy slightly more than the bonding MO is lowered.

neet_che_u03_t12_4.working: A is true: an electron in sigma*1s cancels bonding stabilisation. R is true: sigma*1s is cylindrically symmetric about the axis. However, this symmetry does not explain destabilisation; the node between the nuclei does.

neet_che_u03_t12_5.working: Statement I is false: a sigma orbital has no nodal plane containing the internuclear axis. Statement II is false: bonding electrons concentrate density between the nuclei, which reduces repulsion and stabilises the molecule.
